name: Alar base reduction (alarplasty)
lead: Alar base reduction, usually called alarplasty, is a cosmetic nasal surgery that narrows the width of the nostril flare or the base of the nose by removing small wedges of tissue at the nostril rim or the alar-facial junction. It is performed either on its own or together with rhinoplasty, and surgeons describe it as one of several tools for correcting nostril size and shape.[1][2]

In looksmaxxing culture it is discussed as a hardmaxxing option for people who consider their nostrils too wide or flared. Published literature on the topic consists mainly of surgical technique descriptions and classification studies, including work on how the alar region moves during a smile, rather than controlled trials of cosmetic satisfaction.[3][8]
infobox: Alarplasty, nostril reduction, alar base narrowing

paras: Surgical papers describe alarplasty as excision of a small amount of skin and soft tissue from the nostril sill, the nostril rim or the junction of the nostril wing with the cheek, followed by suturing, to reduce nostril width or flare. A 2001 article on rhinoplasty in patients whose nostrils appear large relative to a small tip proposed analysing the nostril axis and a nostril-to-tip ratio of about 55:45 (with 60:40 considered acceptable), and described the surgical correction as needing more than one component.[1]

A 2026 technique report describes a modified approach in which alar base narrowing and nostril reduction are performed at the same time in Asian rhinoplasty.[5] Surgeons also use alarplasty in functional contexts: one series on external nasal valve collapse used a modified alarplasty combined with columella surgery in severe cases.[6]

A study of a private practice examined how often alarplasty is performed in primary and revision rhinoplasty, indicating that it is a recognised add-on rather than a stand-alone operation in many practices.[7] A 2023 study of 150 Asian women used three-dimensional imaging at rest and during a maximal smile to classify how the alar region changes dynamically, with the aim of informing the choice of alarplasty strategy.[3]

Because the procedure alters the nostril opening, surgeons have examined its effect on breathing. A 2026 cross-sectional study published in Frontiers in Medicine investigated alarplasty and respiratory function.[8] Reports on external nasal valve collapse also note that reducing the nostril opening interacts with airflow, which is why it is discussed alongside functional nasal surgery.[6]

Several PubMed search hits for the term concern veterinary alarplasty in short-nosed dog breeds with airway obstruction; these describe a different species and are not evidence about the cosmetic human procedure.[9]

Human published work includes a classification study of alar dynamics in 150 Asian women,[3] a technique case series for external valve collapse in 37 patients,[6] a practice-based review of how often the procedure is performed,[7] and a 2026 cross-sectional study of respiratory function after alarplasty.[8] No randomised trial comparing cosmetic outcomes with and without alar base reduction was found.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, alarplasty is typically mentioned alongside rhinoplasty in threads where members post before-and-after photographs and ask others to rate the result.[10]

claims.claim: Narrowing the alar base noticeably improves a wide nose
claims.believers: Some users argue that nostril flare is a distinct feature that rhinoplasty alone does not address, and ask for opinions on whether combined rhinoplasty and alarplasty results look better.[10]
claims.experts: Surgical literature treats nostril size and tip proportion as a recognised analysis problem with defined ratios,[1] but no published trial quantifies cosmetic improvement from alar base reduction alone.

claims.claim: The change may be too small to justify surgery for some faces
claims.believers: One commenter in a thread on a posted result said the difference seemed minor relative to the effort involved.[10]
claims.experts: Published studies describe the alar region as varying dynamically with expression, which is why researchers propose individual classification before choosing a technique.[3]

card.summary: Surgery that trims the nostril flare; usually done alongside a nose job, with little trial evidence of its own.
card.aka: Alarplasty, nostril reduction, alar base narrowing
card.note: Alters the nostril opening, so airflow effects have been studied; most literature is technique reports.

quick.overview:
Alar base reduction is a small cosmetic surgery that removes tissue near the nostril wing to make the nostrils narrower or less flared. It is most often combined with rhinoplasty.

On looksmaxxing forums it appears mostly in before-and-after photo threads. Published research is mainly technique descriptions and classification studies rather than trials of how much it improves appearance.
quick.mechanism: Small wedges of skin and soft tissue are removed from the nostril sill or the alar-facial junction and the wound is closed, reducing nostril width.
quick.risks: As a surgical change to the nostril opening, it has been studied for effects on breathing, and some functional nasal surgery reports link nostril reduction to airflow concerns. Scarring and asymmetry are general surgical concerns; no controlled trials of cosmetic outcomes were found.
